narrative.overview:
Kinescope is an evening in front of the screen. The focused title's own artwork fills the canvas and dissolves into a wash of its own colours, so moving focus changes the mood of the room. Everything the app adds sits on top of that picture in one warm off-white and a few steps of its transparency. There is no accent hue in the chrome: focus, progress and the current section are all the same lamplight white, and the only saturated colour on screen comes from the library itself.

The layout is the streaming standard executed with care: a nav line at the top, a hero that follows focus, horizontal rows below, a poster grid for whole libraries, a side sheet for choices. It is dense enough to scan from the couch and calm enough to sit with. Focus is a physical event: the tile lifts 7 percent on a soft static shadow and a white ring hugs it with a 4 px gap. Controls take a full white fill when focused. Both were judged on the household's QN90C on 2026-11-19 and passed ("looks good overall").

The household chose this world over four concept worlds they found too technical. It refuses the black page of thumbnails with a bright ring and a red accent, and borrows nothing from Netflix (name, logo, typeface, the red-on-black signature, profile icons, sounds).
keyCharacteristics: Full-screen title art dissolving into a 2x2 ambience of its own UltraBlur colours, dimmed and slightly desaturated.
One typeface, Mona Sans, in warm off-white with four transparency steps for hierarchy.
No accent hue in chrome. White is the only signal colour.
Focus by lift and a hugging ring on art; by a full white fill on controls.
Motion only in transform and opacity, on a fixed 1920x1080 canvas.

rules.name: The No Accent Rule
rules.body: Chrome carries no hue. Focus, progress, the current section and selection are all Lamplight; colour on screen comes from the artwork and its ambience. A red, coral or brand-coloured ring is a regression.

rules.name: The Room Colour Rule
rules.body: The ambience is Plex's four UltraBlur corner colours painted into a 2x2 WebGL canvas that the compositor stretches to 1920x1080. Each channel becomes `(v + (avg - v) x 0.3) x 0.42`: 30 percent toward its own grey, then dimmed to 42 percent. Fallback corners are `1b1f2b`, `0f1118`, `2a1414`, `0b0d12`. Sign-in and splash use the fixed warm set `6e4a33`, `2c2b33`, `3e2c22`, `1c1d26`. Pushed screens restore the colours the screen under them last set.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Mona Sans for every string. Hierarchy comes from weight, size and the four Lamplight steps, never from a second face or an accent colour.

rules.name: The Couch Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing on screen is smaller than 19 px, and 19 px is only for the tracked uppercase format badges. Every other string is 20 px or larger; second lines under tile captions are 22 px. Legibility is judged on the QN90C from 2.5 to 3.5 m, not on a monitor.

rules.name: The Safe Frame Rule
rules.body: 96 px left and right, 54 px top and bottom. No heading, caption or label in the bottom 54 px (below y 1026). Art may run to the edge; words may not.

rules.name: The Headroom Rule
rules.body: Every clipped list keeps at least `(1.07 - 1) / 2 x tile height + 12` px between its clip edge and its first row's tile top, so the lifted tile and its ring are never cut. That is 21 px for wide and episode tiles, 24 for grid posters, 25 for Home posters, 23 for search posters. The library ships 40.

rules.name: The No Peek Rule
rules.body: Row pitch is chosen so the next row stays below the fold. A heading half on screen at the bottom edge is a defect.

rules.name: The Static Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow is painted once and never animates. The lift's shadow sits on a separate element that appears or fades by opacity; depth on focus comes from scale.

rules.name: The Dissolve Rule
rules.body: The hero dissolves into its own ambience through a static mask. The shipping app A/B-tested hero masks on the TV at 1344x756 at no cost. V1 benches the full-screen size; if it costs frames, the fallback is a stretched raster alpha, not a gradient overlay.

rules.name: The Selected Rule
rules.body: Selected never relies on a fill step alone. A current or set item brings full-white text, usually on a `faint` pill: the current nav entry, the current season, the current settings group, a set chip (whose value also goes to 700 weight). In a sheet, the current choice carries a check at the right edge. Focus always wins over selected.

rules.name: The One Mover Rule
rules.body: In one key press exactly one thing travels: the track or the highlight, never both. In rows the ring is still and the content slides under it.

dos: Do let the focused title's art and its ambience set the colour of the screen; keep chrome in Lamplight and its transparency steps.
Do show focus on art by scale 1.07, the static lift shadow and a 4 px Lamplight ring at a 4 px gap; on controls by a full white fill with `on-text` (#151413) text.
Do keep the row ring fixed at x 96 and slide the content under it.
Do mark selected or current items with full-white text (on a `faint` pill) or a check, never with a fill step alone.
Do keep 96 px side margins, the nav at y 56, and every heading, caption and label above y 1026.
Do leave `(1.07 - 1) / 2 x tile height + 12` px of headroom above the first row of any clipped list.
Do use row pitch 464 for wide rows and 500 for poster rows on Home, so the next row stays below the fold.
Do build skeletons at the exact geometry of the content they stand for.
Do keep voice plain and warm; allow a little personality in empty and error lines only.
donts: Don't add an accent hue to the chrome: no coral, no red, no brand colour on rings, progress, badges or the current section.
Don't borrow from Netflix: its name, logo, typeface, red-on-black signature, profile icons or sounds.
Don't put a Plex mark in the product name or the SamSUCKS mascot anywhere.
Don't show permanent key-hint text; hints appear in context and fade.
Don't let the next row's heading peek at the bottom edge.
Don't use a second typeface or a system display face.
Don't blur, frost or glow anything, and don't animate a shadow.
Don't paint ambience or scrims with full-screen CSS gradients.
Don't show the upstream credit in the chrome; it lives in About.
